audit_findings.root_cause: persistent_workers=True with new DataLoader created per training call

root_cause_detail.pattern: DataLoader created per-call → goes out of scope → persistent workers not reaped by parent

audit_findings.missing_evidence: Cannot confirm zero zombies until trainer naturally restarts (protected runtime — cannot restart PID 1037427)

fixes_applied.detail: Workers now terminate when DataLoader is released, not kept alive across training calls

fixes_applied.fix: Worker count capped at 4 via compute_dataloader_workers()
fixes_applied.old_formula: max(1, min(32, cpu_count-2)) — could spawn 30 on 32-core machine

fixes_applied.detail: RTX 5080 saturates memory bus at low worker counts; 2 is sufficient

fixes_applied.fix: Explicit del loader in finally block
fixes_applied.detail: Ensures DataLoader is garbage-collected before next training call, releasing workers promptly even if exception occurs

fixes_applied.fix: Extracted worker config to standalone module

logging_note: Phase 5 fix note: active worker count, batch latency, GPU utilization per-pool logging is recorded via existing PPOTrainingResult fields (dataloader_workers, vram_allocated_mb, training_steps_per_minute). Dedicated worker health telemetry is served by the existing trainer_worker_health service.
validation_note: Fix takes effect on next trainer restart. Current 19 zombies under PID 1037427 are kernel-harmless (Z state, zero CPU/memory) and will be reaped when trainer process exits. Cannot restart trainer per protected runtime policy.
